title: Braised Chickpeas with Fennel, Olives & Preserved Lemon
subtitle: Recipe Formulation Sheet

meta.reconstruction: **This sheet is the least source-anchored in the archive.** The original document is a descriptive overview of the dish rather than a recipe — it states only the chickpea can size, an oven temperature, a rough cook time, and the harissa quantity for one variation. Every other mass, ratio, and timing below is a standard-proportion reconstruction for this style of braise, not a figure carried over from a source. Treat the matrix as a starting point to cook against and revise, and expect to adjust the fennel-to-chickpea ratio and the salt to your own preserved lemon and olives, which vary enormously in intensity.

summary: A savory, tender Mediterranean braise. Slow-cooked or oven-braised, the fennel turns tender while the chickpeas absorb the briny olives and citrus-forward preserved lemon. Typically seasoned with garlic, herbs, and paprika, and served with crusty bread or over couscous.
scalingPrinciple: Item A.01 (Drained Chickpeas) is locked at 100.0% as the substrate baseline. Because this formulation is reconstructed rather than source-derived, the percentages here describe a workable starting ratio rather than a validated specification — the fennel-to-chickpea relationship in particular is the main axis worth tuning across batches.

rows.name: Chickpeas, drained
rows.role: Primary substrate. Canned gives an easy, robust texture; drained weight varies by brand.

rows.name: Fennel Bulbs, quartered
rows.role: Seared in olive oil to build flavor, then braised until tender. The dominant vegetable mass.

rows.name: Olives (Castelvetrano or oil-cured), pitted
rows.role: Briny counterweight to the fennel's sweetness.

rows.name: Preserved Lemon Rind, finely diced
rows.role: Complex salty-sour tang. Rind only — discard the pulp.

rows.name: Extra-Virgin Olive Oil
rows.role: Searing fat and braising medium; also the sauce body.

rows.name: Harissa Paste (variation)
rows.role: For the spicy harissa-braised variation. Source-stated quantity.

rows.name: Fresh Dill, Parsley, or Marjoram
rows.role: Folded in raw at the end for a bright finish.

rows.name: Salt and Pepper
rows.role: Season late — preserved lemon and olives both carry significant salt.

total.role: Combined raw material input footprint, excluding seasoning.

matrixFootnote: *Every mass in this matrix except the harissa is a reconstructed estimate. The source states only "one 15-ounce can (drained)" of chickpeas, 1.5 tablespoons of harissa for the spicy variation, and a 375°F / ~1 hour braise. All quantities are marked accordingly.

mise.label: Fennel (B.01)
mise.text: Trim the stalks, reserving any fronds for the finish. Quarter the bulbs through the root so the layers stay attached during searing.

mise.label: Preserved Lemon (C.02)
mise.text: Separate rind from pulp. Discard the pulp and finely dice the rind only — the pulp is aggressively salty and turns the braise one-note.

mise.label: Olives (C.01)
mise.text: Pit if not already pitted. Leave whole or halve depending on preference.

execution.name: Sear the Fennel
execution.text: Heat the olive oil in a Dutch oven. Sear the quartered fennel cut-side down until well browned on the cut faces. This browning is the flavor base of the dish — do not rush it or crowd the pan.

execution.name: Bloom Aromatics
execution.text: Add the sliced garlic and fennel seeds (and harissa, if making the spicy variation) and cook until fragrant.

execution.name: Combine and Cover
execution.text: Add the drained chickpeas, olives, and diced preserved lemon rind. Stir to combine and add a splash of water or stock if the pan looks dry. Cover.

execution.name: Braise
execution.text: Transfer the covered Dutch oven, or a covered baking dish, to the oven. Braise until the fennel is completely tender and the chickpeas have absorbed the briny, citrus-forward liquid.

execution.name: Finish
execution.text: Taste and season with salt and pepper — late, once the olive and preserved lemon salt has distributed. Top with fresh dill, parsley, or marjoram.

alternatives.label: Harissa Olive Oil-Braised:
alternatives.text: A popular, spicy variation using 1 1/2 tablespoons of harissa paste for heat, bloomed with the garlic in step 2.

alternatives.label: Cheesy Addition:
alternatives.text: Incorporate feta during the final 10–15 minutes of cooking for a salty, creamy element. No longer vegan.

alternatives.label: Serving:
alternatives.text: Serve with warm crusty bread to soak up the olive oil and broth, or over fluffy couscous, quinoa, or polenta. Top with plain yogurt or labneh for extra creaminess.

directive: Season at the very end, never at the start. Preserved lemon and cured olives both release substantial salt across an hour-long braise, and a dish salted to taste at the beginning will be inedible by the time it comes out of the oven.
